title: For Thy Mercy and Thy Grace
description: For Thy Mercy and Thy Grace in Tonic Solfa to ST. BEES, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Downton wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 168.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BEES; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: For Thy mer-cy and Thy grace, Con-stant through an-oth-er year, Hear our song of thank-ful-ness; Je-sus, our Re-deem-er, hear!

lines: For Thy mercy and Thy grace,
Constant through another year,
Hear our song of thankfulness;
Jesus, our Redeemer, hear!
Lo! our sins on Thee we cast,
Thee, our perfect Sacrifice,
And, forgetting all the past,
Press unto our glorious prize.
Dark the future; let Thy light
Guide us, bright and Morning Star:
Fierce our foes and hard the fight;
Arm us, Savior, for the war.
In our weakness and distress,
Rock of strength, be Thou our Stay;
In the pathless wilderness
Be our true and living Way.
Who of us death’s awful road
In the coming year shall tread?
With Thy rod and staff, O God,
Comfort Thou his dying bed.
Keep us faithful, keep us pure,
Keep us evermore Thine own;
Help, O help us to endure;
Fit us for the promised crown.
So within Thy palace gate
We shall praise, on golden strings,
Thee the only Potentate,
Lord of lords and King of kings.

licence: Public domain: Henry Downton died in 1885.
credits: Words by Henry Downton (1818–1885), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. BEES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
